detailedSteps.title: Paper Preprocessing & Structured Parsing
detailedSteps.desc: Frontier LLM performs section-aware paper decomposition, splitting abstract, methods, experiments, and conclusions, outputting structured summaries, core concept lists, and key entity-relation candidate sets

detailedSteps.title: Domain Expert Deep Reading & Understanding
detailedSteps.desc: Matching perfectly aligned domain experts (PhD-level+) from expert pool, focusing on methodological details, implicit assumptions, academic lineage, and knowledge boundaries in the paper

detailedSteps.title: Collaborative Knowledge Graph Construction
detailedSteps.desc: AI extracts entity-relation-entity triples using ontology-guided + section-aware prompting from AutoQG paper. Human experts review, supplement omissions, and distinguish explicit vs implicit association graphs requiring domain knowledge

detailedSteps.title: High-Discriminative Question Design via Reasoning Chains
detailedSteps.desc: Based on multi-hop reasoning paths in knowledge graphs combined with expert domain knowledge, design high-discriminative questions with complex reasoning chains near disciplinary boundaries

detailedSteps.title: AI Difficulty Calibration & Consistency Verification
detailedSteps.desc: Frontier models cross-verify question difficulty: send questions all models can answer back for revision, send questions all models get wrong for human verification of answer correctness

detailedSteps.title: Multi-expert Cross-Blind Review
detailedSteps.desc: Double-blind review protocol: each question scored by at least three independent experts across relevance, answerability, distractor quality, fluency, reasoning depth, evidence traceability, with automatic reliability testing

detailedSteps.title: Final Decision & Data Ingestion
detailedSteps.desc: Based on disciplinary balance, difficulty gradient, question type, and other concerns, senior experts make final decision on ingestion

hle.name: HLE
hle.desc: High-level multimodal expert reasoning dataset built by a Tsinghua University expert team of ~100 active masters/PhD students through a human-in-the-loop system, with high-quality reasoning chains and MAS multi-layer quality verification.
hle.brief: HLE (Hard-Level Evaluation) is a high-difficulty scientific reasoning benchmark for frontier LLMs. Questions are designed and reviewed by domain experts across 12+ disciplines, requiring deep reasoning rather than surface matching. Each question includes complete reasoning chain annotations and difficulty ratings.
hle.structure:
{
  "query": "Under standard conditions, which reaction has the most negative ΔG°?",
  "rubric": "Correct option plus thermodynamic derivation required",
  "answer": "Option C, reasoning chain: ...",
  "domain": "chemistry",
  "difficulty": 4
}

math-hard.name: Hard Math Problems
math-hard.desc: Text-based dataset for hard mathematical reasoning covering analysis, algebra, number theory and geometry, with problem statements, full solutions and answers — for training and evaluating multi-step proof, symbolic reasoning and answer generation.
math-hard.brief: Each problem is written by mathematics experts with a complete solution process, emphasizing multi-step proof and symbolic manipulation. Suitable as training data and as a high-discrimination evaluation set for mathematical reasoning.
math-hard.structure:
{
  "problem": "Prove: for every positive integer n, ...",
  "field": "number_theory",
  "solution": "By induction on the base case...",
  "answer": "...",
  "difficulty": 5
}

sfe.name: SFE
sfe.desc: SFE benchmark for evaluating MLLM scientific cognition from perception to reasoning. Data created by professors (associate level and above) and senior grad students from Tsinghua and other top-985 universities based on their research experience, covering 5 disciplines (astronomy, chemistry, earth science, life science, materials science).
sfe.brief: SFE benchmark for evaluating MLLM scientific cognition from perception to reasoning. Data created by professors (associate level and above) and senior grad students from Tsinghua and other top-985 universities based on their research experience, covering 5 disciplines (astronomy, chemistry, earth science, life science, materials science).
sfe.structure:
{
  "question": "Identify the sample phase from the XRD pattern...",
  "image": "xrd_pattern.png",
  "answer": "...",
  "discipline": "materials",
  "level": "expert"
}

stem-video.name: STEM Video Reasoning
stem-video.desc: Expert-built STEM video understanding dataset evaluating deep reasoning and knowledge association over science/engineering teaching and experiment videos.
stem-video.brief: Videos come from real STEM teaching and lab scenarios. Questions emphasize reasoning over dynamic processes, experimental phenomena and disciplinary knowledge rather than simple content description.

crosslingual-k12-stem.name: Cross-lingual K12 & University STEM
crosslingual-k12-stem.desc: Multi-lingual STEM dataset for K12 and university levels, covering math, physics, chemistry and biology — improving subject reasoning in multilingual education scenarios.
crosslingual-k12-stem.brief: Questions collected from official textbooks and exercise books across countries, verified in multiple rounds by native-speaking education experts to preserve original logic and cultural context. Covers 20+ languages.

sci-infograph.name: Sci Infograph
sci-infograph.desc: Infographic dataset for STEM textbook scenarios — math, physics, chemistry, biology, geoscience and engineering diagrams — evaluating comprehension of scientific figures, annotations, processes, structural relations and text-image information.
sci-infograph.brief: Covers textbook illustrations, lab apparatus diagrams, process schematics and more, focusing on joint text-image understanding and structural relation reasoning.

microvqa.name: MicroVQA
microvqa.desc: Microscopy VQA dataset aiding scientific discovery — focusing on microscopic images and cellular structures with high difficulty — improving models' scientific image understanding.
microvqa.brief: QA over microscopy images requires professional biology background and microstructure recognition — a high-difficulty evaluation set for scientific image understanding.

msearth.name: MSEarth
msearth.desc: QA dataset for niche geoscience disciplines (geography, geology, seismology, oceanography), expert-built around professional image reasoning with high difficulty — improving scientific image understanding.
msearth.brief: Covers multiple niche geoscience fields. Questions revolve around geological sections, seismic phase diagrams, nautical charts and other professional images, evaluating image reasoning on long-tail disciplines.

proactive-video.name: Streaming Video Proactive Response
proactive-video.desc: Evaluates whether models can respond at the right moment in streaming video input. Fully expert-built (pure human work, beyond model capability), multi-round proofread, durations from 15s to 30min, diverse scenes and tasks.
proactive-video.brief: Each sample annotates the optimal response timing and content within the stream, training models from passive answering to proactive interaction — frontier data for the proactive direction.

multimodal-av.name: Multimodal AV Alignment (Expert-verified)
multimodal-av.desc: Professional audio-video description, analysis and alignment dataset built mainly by music and film experts. Every slice, description and QA pair is created in EntropyOrder's proprietary human-in-the-loop system with fine-grained audio and comprehensive video descriptions.
multimodal-av.brief: Audio-side annotations include fine-grained instrumentation, emotion and musical form; video-side covers shots, scenes and narrative elements. QA cross-verified by multiple models. For AV joint understanding training and evaluation.

camera-motion.name: Camera Motion Dataset
camera-motion.desc: Frame-by-frame camera motion dataset, manually annotated at fine granularity (6fps) in EntropyOrder's proprietary annotation system with double-check and clear spatial localization.
camera-motion.brief: Frame-level (6fps) annotations of camera motion type, direction and intensity — high-precision supervision for camera control in video generation and shot-language parsing in video understanding.

crosslingual-multimodal.name: Cross-lingual Multimodal Multi-task Evaluation
crosslingual-multimodal.desc: Comprehensive evaluation dataset built by minority-language students and teachers, covering multiple languages and multimodal input formats with diverse task types — systematically evaluating multimodal understanding and generalization in cross-lingual scenarios.
crosslingual-multimodal.brief: Built directly by native speakers of low-resource languages rather than translated. Tasks include multiple choice, fill-in-blank and open QA, truly reflecting model capability in low-resource scenarios.

misleading-images.name: Misleading Images: Mirror & Contour
misleading-images.desc: Manually built mirror and contour recognition dataset, designed specifically for MLLMs' weaknesses in color perception, contour perception and spatial awareness.
misleading-images.brief: Systematically constructed misleading samples targeting known MLLM perceptual weaknesses (mirroring, contours, spatial relations) — for locating and fixing low-level visual perception errors.

infograph.name: InfoGraph
infograph.desc: Infographic understanding dataset combining web crawling, expert construction and expert review — covering charts, flow diagrams, statistics graphics and more — evaluating interpretation and reasoning over complex visual information.
infograph.brief: Three data pipelines (crawl + build + review) ensure both scale and quality. Questions emphasize value reading, trend judgment and cross-figure reasoning.

art.name: Art Appreciation Dataset
art.desc: Expert-built art appreciation dataset covering Western painting, sculpture, porcelain, pottery, sketching, murals, photography, printmaking, textiles, installation art and calligraphy — each piece with HD multimodal materials and 1-3 expert appreciations.
art.brief: Appreciation texts written by art history experts, covering stylistic lineage, technique analysis and aesthetic judgment — training models for art understanding and professional expression.

yukicoder-extension.name: Yukicoder Extension
yukicoder-extension.desc: High-difficulty competitive programming dataset for RL code training — extending yukicoder problems with testcases, submissions, checkers/interactors, verified by sandbox judging and HITL quality inspection.
yukicoder-extension.brief: Each problem is extended with high-quality test cases and standard checkers, ready to plug into RL pipelines with stable reward signals — ideal for reinforcement learning of code reasoning.

scicode.name: SciCode
scicode.desc: Scientific computing code generation and numerical reasoning dataset covering reaction-diffusion, molecular dynamics, ecological dynamical systems and more — each problem includes background, function interface, subtasks, canonical solution, test cases and validation report.
scicode.brief: Problems come from real research scenarios, requiring models to understand scientific formulas and produce numerically verifiable code — evaluating both scientific comprehension and engineering implementation.

oj-competition.name: OJ Competition Extension
oj-competition.desc: Premium competition problems where seed-2.0-pro pass@2 = 0, expert-built with ~1000 additional testcases per problem for comprehensive difficulty evaluation, plus updated submissions.
oj-competition.brief: Filters competition problems that the strongest current model fails in both samples, each with 1000+ test cases and updated submissions — a hard ceiling for code capability evaluation.

openclaw.name: OpenClaw Trajectories
openclaw.desc: Records OpenClaw operation trajectories in structured tasks, including complete workspace, sessions and more — training and evaluating planning, execution and error-correction for agent capability building.
openclaw.brief: Trajectories fully preserve task context, tool call sequences and intermediate states, supporting multiple agent training paradigms such as behavior cloning and process reward modeling.

agentos-trajectory.name: AgentOS Trajectory
agentos-trajectory.desc: Multi-turn, long-horizon tool-calling trajectory dataset for AgentOS scenarios — with call-level raw request/response, code session event streams and structured task traces — training and evaluating planning, tool use, execution correction and complex task delivery.
agentos-trajectory.brief: Call-level granularity of real user-AgentOS interactions. Long-horizon tasks cover multi-tool coordination and mid-course correction — core data for training delivery-oriented agents.

gdpval-extension.name: GDPval Extension
gdpval-extension.desc: Agent tool-calling trajectory dataset for real business scenarios — financial compliance, HR, cloud computing, retail operations, tax accounting — including query, attachments, expert deliverables, rubrics, multi-model traces and final deliverables.
gdpval-extension.brief: Gold-standard real industry deliverables with multi-model trace comparison revealing capability gaps. Rubric-based evaluation directly applicable to benchmarking agent business-delivery capability.

skillbench.name: SkillBench
skillbench.desc: End-to-end task dataset for agent skill evaluation and training — real business scenarios in finance, legal, security, audit — including task description, environment, data, tests, canonical solutions and execution traces.
skillbench.brief: Each task packages a complete execution environment with runnable tests, plus both canonical solution and expert traces — usable both as a skill benchmark and as SFT/RL training data.

search-retrieval.name: Information Retrieval Data
search-retrieval.desc: Long-chain information reasoning and retrieval data built two ways: expert-curated multi-hop (>5 hops) questions from internet corners, and expert-distilled fuzzy retrieval needs from real users — ensuring diversity.
search-retrieval.brief: Dual-channel construction of multi-hop retrieval chains and real fuzzy needs, double-checked by prompted LLM and humans — training deep retrieval and evidence integration in open-web environments.

open-challenge.name: Open-ended Real-world Retrieval Challenges
open-challenge.desc: Reasoning, retrieval and evaluation dataset for complex real-world scenarios — carefully designed single/multi-turn retrieval questions requiring industry expert-level knowledge, as encountered by real users.
open-challenge.brief: Questions come from real expert-level retrieval challenges faced by users, in single and multi-turn forms — evaluating the full chain of retrieval, reasoning and answer evaluation under complex real-world constraints.
